title: Eli Lilly acquires LoQus23 in US$725M deal to advance Huntington’s disease treatment | HealthCare Middle East & Africa - No.1 Health & Pharma Manufacturing Industry Publication
summary: An estimated 75,000 people across the US, UK, and Europe live with Huntington’s disease
thbAction: Use the article as an entry point to pitch THB's commercial visibility layer for territory planning, account prioritization, and next-best-action for pharma leadership teams.
contentHtml:
USA— Eli Lilly has agreed to acquire British biotechnology company LoQus23 Therapeutics for up to US$725 million in upfront and milestone payments, strengthening its neuroscience pipeline as competition to develop disease-modifying treatments for Huntington’s disease intensifies.

The acquisition gives Lilly access to LoQus23’s preclinical small-molecule pipeline, which targets the expansion of DNA triplet repeats associated with genetic disorders, including Huntington’s disease and myotonic dystrophy type 1

The deal centres on LQT-23, LoQus23’s lead oral candidate.

The drug selectively and indirectly inhibits MutS Homolog 3 (MSH3), a protein involved in DNA mismatch repair that researchers believe contributes to the progression of Huntington’s disease.

According to LoQus23, preclinical studies have shown that LQT-23 can block somatic expansion, the process through which repeated DNA sequences increase in length in affected cells over time.

The company has demonstrated these effects in relevant cell and animal models, supporting further development of the candidate as a potential disease-modifying treatment.

LoQus23 plans to submit a clinical trial application for LQT-23 in the near future.

If successful, the programme could advance into human studies and provide another approach to treating a condition that currently has no approved disease-modifying therapies.

Competition for Huntington’s disease treatments

An estimated 75,000 people across the US, UK, and Europe live with Huntington’s disease, a progressive, inherited neurodegenerative disorder that affects movement, cognition and behaviour.

The disease typically leads to death 15 to 20 years after symptom onset.

Several biotechnology companies are pursuing treatments that could slow or modify its progression.

Dutch biotech UniQure has advanced its gene therapy AMT-130 into regulatory review in the US after navigating several regulatory challenges.

The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has set May 1, 2027, as its target action date for the application.

Meanwhile, Lineage Cell Therapeutics recently acquired NeuroArmid Therapeutics, gaining access to a clinical-stage programme designed to support neural network formation.

LoQus23 also attracted investment from Novartis’ venture capital arm, which participated in the British biotech’s seed and Series A financing rounds.

Commenting on the acquisition, LoQus23 Chief Executive Officer David Reynolds said Lilly’s neuroscience expertise and development capabilities would help accelerate LQT-23 through clinical development.

Lilly expands biotechnology acquisitions

The transaction adds to Lilly’s growing acquisition and licensing activity in 2026 as the pharmaceutical company expands beyond its established metabolic disease portfolio.

Its weight-loss and diabetes franchise, led by tirzepatide, continues to generate substantial revenue.

In its latest dealmaking activity, Lilly agreed to acquire hematology-focused biotech Calytrix Bio for US$1.5 billion and entered a US$5.9 billion cancer drug licensing agreement with Stipple Bio on the same day.

The LoQus23 acquisition also comes amid increased investment and consolidation in the British biotechnology sector.

Recent high-profile exits include Centessa Pharmaceuticals, Silence Therapeutics, Myricx Bio, and Dark Blue Therapeutics.

Funding activity has also gained momentum, with UK-based artificial intelligence drug discovery company Isomorphic Labs securing US$5 billion in financing.

A recent report by the BioIndustry Association (BIA) indicated that the UK biotechnology sector was on track to record its strongest year for venture capital investment since 2021.
